You are mapping the existing codebase surface that a PDP (product detail page) build must integrate with, so that a takeover of an in-flight PR reuses what exists instead of rebuilding it. READ-ONLY. Do NOT modify files, do NOT commit, do NOT run `npm start`.

Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
Branch (checked out): feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information

YOUR TASK:

1. WHAT EXISTS FOR PDP ALREADY. Map:
   - overrides/app/pages/product-detail/ — read it fully. What does the page currently render, what data does it fetch, what components does it compose?
   - The base SFCC version at node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/ — what is in the base that we have or have not overridden?
   - Existing PDP-adjacent component overrides: overrides/app/components/image-gallery/, swatch-group/, display-price/, product-tile/, product-item/, recommended-products/, product-view/ (if present), quantity-picker. For each: does an override exist, and does it have a theme recipe in overrides/app/theme/components/?

2. THE COMPONENT STRUCTURE CONVENTION. The settled convention in this repo is:
   overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
   with styling ALWAYS via a theme recipe in overrides/app/theme/components/, registered in that folder's index.ts.
   - List what actually exists under overrides/app/components/ui-kits/ today (I believe only a handful of directories exist).
   - Report the naming families in play so they are not confused: SFCC override dirs are kebab-case (product-tile/), ui-kit components are camelCase (zimmButton/), shared/ui primitives are PascalCase (Button/).
   - Read .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md and any .claude/rules/overrides.md for the authoritative statement, and report where the branch's code diverges.

3. THE COMPONENT REGISTRY. There is a `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` and related registry work (recently active on branch feature/f2r-component-registry, 31 commits ahead). Determine:
   - What the registry is for and whether a new PDP component is expected to register itself.
   - Whether the registry exists on THIS branch or only on the f2r branch — i.e. whether it is a dependency we would be building against something not yet merged to develop.

4. THREE OVERRIDE INTERCEPT TRAPS — verify whether any apply to the PDP work:
   a. The `ccExtensibility` resolver that redirects `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to overrides/ runs ONLY in the real webpack build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to node_modules and vitest.config.ts does not touch it. So importing an ALREADY-OVERRIDDEN component by its base path renders/tests the UNSTYLED BASE version in Storybook and Vitest while working correctly in the app. Grep the PDP code for base-path imports of components that have local overrides.
   b. A relative re-export inside a barrel is not rewritten by the resolver. Check overrides/app/components/shared/ui/ — if the base barrel re-exports './Button' relatively and 208 base files import the barrel rather than the deep path, then overriding shared/ui/<Name> intercepts nothing. Verify whether the PDP work depends on this.
   c. Conditional render of an alternate module: e.g. base _app/index.jsx renders <CheckoutFooter/> instead of <Footer/> on checkout, so overriding footer does not reach /checkout. Check whether PDP has any equivalent conditional-swap that would bypass an override.

5. DATA LAYER. The rule is that components under overrides/app/components/ receive data as props and do NOT call data-fetching hooks; fetching belongs in overrides/app/pages/. Report how product data currently reaches the PDP (which hook, in which file) and what shape it is, so new components can be typed against it. Note the project rule: no mocking in production paths, all data from live Commerce Cloud API via @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react.

6. TESTING HARNESS REALITY. Report accurately (this has been got wrong before):
   - Storybook a11y IS CI-gated: @storybook/test-runner reads parameters.a11y.test and .storybook/preview.tsx sets it to "error". There is no .storybook/test-runner.js and none is needed. Confirm this is still true by reading .storybook/preview.tsx and package.json.
   - Confirm what IS and IS NOT gated in .github/workflows/qa.yml — specifically whether eslint, prettier, and tsc --noEmit are gated anywhere.
   - Report which test layers a new PDP component is actually required to have per .claude/rules/testing.md.

OUTPUT: Write to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/4447dd18-bbe0-4a85-aae2-6e8935bf7947/scratchpad/conventions.md

Structure:
- PDP surface that already exists (page, components, recipes) — a table
- What a new PDP component must look like structurally, per the rules, with a concrete path example
- Registry: what it is, whether it is available on this branch, and whether it is a blocker
- Intercept traps: which apply here, with evidence
- Data layer: how product data reaches the page, with the type
- Test requirements for this work, and what CI will actually enforce
- REUSE OPPORTUNITIES: things the PDP build should be using that already exist

Then give a condensed version in your final report. Cite file:line throughout, and distinguish what you verified from what you inferred.

     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Pre-commit hook:
     3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
     4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
     5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
     6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
     7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
     8	#
     9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
    10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
    11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
    12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
    14	
    15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
    17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
    18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
    19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
    20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21	
    22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
    24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
    25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
    26	
    27	  # fnm
    28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
    30	  fi
    31	
    32	  # volta
    33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
    35	  fi
    36	
    37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    40	    exit 1
    41	  fi
    42	fi
    43	
    44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
    46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48	
    49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
    50	
    51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
    52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
    53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
    54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
    55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

    58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
    59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
    60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
    61	  git add .claude/registry/
    62	fi
    63

    65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate

    69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Override Components — Pre-flight Rules

Rules for every file under `overrides/app/components/` that shadows an SFCC base module.
Distilled from the Link override build (`feature/f2r-component-registry`, 2026-08-14).
Cross-referenced from [components.md](./components.md).

---

## The override system is replacement, not wrapping

When a file exists at `overrides/app/components/<name>/`, the Salesforce PWA Kit's webpack
resolver routes **every import** of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>`
to that override — including imports inside SFCC's own base components (cart, checkout,
product tile, footer, account pages, etc.).

This means:
- An override is a full module replacement, not a decorator around the original.
- It must be self-contained: **an override cannot import from its own path** — that
  resolves circularly back to itself.
- It must be a complete, API-compatible drop-in for every caller that already uses the
  SFCC original, not just Zimmermann pages.

---

## Pre-flight checks — run before writing any code

### 1. Read the SFCC source exports

Open `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>/index.jsx` and note:
- Is there an `export default`? → The override **must** have one too.
- Are there named exports? → Replicate them.

A missing `export default` silently makes every SFCC base component that imports this
module render `undefined` — with no runtime error, only webpack warnings buried in output.

### 2. Check for internal SFCC usage

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/ --include="*.jsx" --include="*.js" | head
```

If results appear, the component is a **shared internal dependency** — it is imported by
SFCC base components, not just Zimmermann pages. The override must be self-contained (no
import from its own override path) and must replicate the full export shape.

If no results: the component is a **leaf component** — lower risk. A named-export-only
override with no default export will not break SFCC internals (though matching the export
shape is still good practice).

### 3. Check behavioral contracts

Does the SFCC original use `React.forwardRef`? → The override's default export must too.

Omitting `forwardRef` silently returns `null` for any ref attached to the component.
This breaks focus management (WCAG 2.2 AA requirement) and any animation library that
uses refs, without any console error or TypeScript warning.

### 4. For theme component configs — audit Chakra's defaults

If the component has a `theme/components/<name>.ts` file that extends a Chakra built-in
(Button, Input, Link, etc.), there is an equivalent pre-flight: Chakra's `defineStyleConfig`
deep-merges with the built-in's defaults rather than replacing them, so properties Chakra
already defines will silently survive and override your `textStyle` expansions. Audit Chakra's
defaults before writing the config. Full details and the audit command are in
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) > "Overriding a Chakra built-in — audit before
relying on textStyle".

---

## Prop superset rule

The override must accept **all props the SFCC original accepts**, and may add
Zimmermann-specific props on top. No SFCC prop may be silently dropped.

**Pattern:**
- **Default export** — API-compatible drop-in. Props at least as wide as the SFCC original.
  Used by SFCC base components; should not enforce Zimmermann-specific defaults.
- **Named export** — Zimmermann-branded wrapper around the default export. Adds narrowed
  variant types, brand-specific defaults, JSDoc. Used by Zimmermann pages and components.

```tsx
// Default export: SFCC-compatible, full prop surface, forwardRef preserved
const BaseName = React.forwardRef<HTMLElement, BaseProps>(({ ...all sfcc props... }, ref) => { ... });
BaseName.displayName = 'Name';
export default BaseName;

// Named export: Zimmermann additions layered on top
export const Name = React.forwardRef<HTMLElement, ZimmProps>(
  ({ variant = 'lg', ...rest }, ref) => <BaseName ref={ref} variant={variant} {...rest} />
);
Name.displayName = 'Name';
```

`Link` (named, adds `variant?: 'lg' | 'sm'` with default `'lg'`).

When the override needs to import from a module that already has a `declare module` block
in `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`, check that declaration before anything else.

  as `__css={styles.<part>}` (`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:27, 32`).
- Recipe declares `parts: ['name','price','description','modelInfo','styleCode']` and a `baseStyle`
  per part (`theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts:56-90`).
- Values that genuinely can't live in `baseStyle` (conditional margins) are exported as named consts

**Chakra scale caveat (matters for any new recipe):** `theme/index.ts:51-58` registers only
`borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles, components`. `fontSizes`, `sizes`, and

for different values (`theme/index.ts:26-49`). So `fontSize="2xs"` in a recipe silently resolves to
Chakra's 10px, not Zimmermann's 14px — which is exactly why `pdpProductInfo.ts` uses
`fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)'`. `spacing` **is** registered as `space`, so `marginBottom: 'l'`
is safe. **[V]**

## 4. Intercept traps — which apply

### (a) base-path import → unstyled base component in Storybook & Vitest

**Mechanism confirmed [V]:**
- `package.json` `ccExtensibility: {extends: '@salesforce/retail-react-app', overridesDir: 'overrides'}`
  — read by the pwa-kit webpack plugin, i.e. **real builds only**.
- `.storybook/main.js:25` aliases `'@salesforce/retail-react-app'` → `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app`,
  bypassing the resolver entirely.
- `vitest.config.ts:17-20` aliases only `~` and `app` — it never mentions
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, so those imports go straight to `node_modules` by normal resolution.

**Does it apply to the PDP work today? Not yet.** I cross-referenced every base-path import in
`overrides/` against every existing override directory. The **only** collision in the entire repo is
`icons`, and it is deliberate (`overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx:73` re-exports from the base
icon set — that's the documented single-source-of-truth pattern; `header/index.tsx:44` imports the
same base path). **[V]**

Every other base-path import in `overrides/` resolves to a module we do **not** override
(`shared/ui`, `constants`, `contexts`, `utils/*`, `seo`, `link`, `loading-spinner`, `search`,
`with-registration`, `product-scroller`, `section`, `hooks/use-multi-site`, `hooks/use-current-basket`,
`hooks/use-navigation`, `hooks/use-einstein`, `app/theme`, `app/routes`, `app/mocks/standard-product`).
Per `overrideStyling.md` that is simply correct. **[V]**

**It becomes live the moment PDP work adds an override.** Concretely: if you create
`overrides/app/components/swatch-group/`, then `product-view/index.jsx:55` imports it by base path —
correct in the app, base-unstyled in Storybook/Vitest. Same for `image-gallery` (`product-view:44,48`),
`display-price` (`product-view:53` + 5 others), `quantity-picker` (`product-view:50`),
`breadcrumb` (**already overridden**, and `product-view/index.jsx:45` imports it by base path — so the
moment anything writes a story or test that renders base `ProductView`, it will render the *base*
breadcrumb, not ours). **[V]**

Rule for new PDP code, per `overrideStyling.md` > "Importing an already-overridden component":
import an already-overridden sibling by **relative path** (`'../breadcrumb'`), never by base path. The
PDP page already does this correctly at `index.tsx:6,8,9` (all relative `../../components/…`). **[V]**

### (b) `shared/ui` barrel — a relative re-export the resolver never rewrites

**Confirmed with hard numbers [V]:**
- `node_modules/…/app/components/shared/ui/index.jsx` is a pure barrel of **103** relative re-exports
  (`export {Box} from './Box'`, `export {Button} from './Button'`, …).
- Base files importing the barrel path `…/components/shared/ui'`: **212**.
- Base files importing a deep `…/components/shared/ui/<Name>` path: **0**.

Because the re-export is relative (`'./Button'`), the `ccExtensibility` resolver — which only rewrites
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers — never sees it. Creating
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/Button/index.tsx` would intercept **zero** of those 212 consumers.
You would additionally have to override the barrel itself.

re-exports (`shared/ui/Skeleton/index.jsx` is literally `export {Skeleton} from '@chakra-ui/react'`) —
there is nothing to override there. No `overrides/app/components/shared/` exists on HEAD or `develop`
(`git ls-tree` = 0 on both). The correct lever for `Box`/`Text`/`Skeleton` styling is the Chakra theme,
which is already how the repo does it. **[V]**

while `product-detail/index.tsx:5` and `zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:3` import them from the SFCC

## 5. Data layer

**Rule** (`.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition): anything under `overrides/app/components/`
receives data as props and calls **no** data-fetching hook — not `useProduct`, not any
`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook. Fetching lives in `overrides/app/pages/`. **[V]**

**The PDP obeys this today** — `useProduct`/`useCategory` are called only in
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:21-31`; `PdpProductInfo`, `Breadcrumb` and
`ZimmPageToolbar` are all pure prop-driven. **[V]**

**Type chain [V]:**

```
useProduct  →  node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.d.ts:28
               UseQueryResult<DataType<Client['getProduct']>>
            →  commerce-sdk-isomorphic ShopperProductsModelTypes.Product
               (node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835)
```

Fields the PDP already reads, all optional on the type: `id: string` (the only required one), `name?`,
`price?`, `currency?`, `shortDescription?`, `longDescription?`, `primaryCategoryId?`. Also available and
unused: `imageGroups?: Array<ImageGroup>`, `variants?`, `variationAttributes?`, `variationValues?`,
`master?`, `inventory?`/`inventories?`, `type?: ProductType`, `setProducts?`, `bundledProducts?`,
`productPromotions?`, `priceRanges?`, `prices?`, `pageMetaTags?`, `slugUrl?`. **[V]**

**Custom SFCC attributes.** The type ends in `& { [key: string]: any }` (`index.esm.d.ts:59834`), so any
`c_*` attribute typechecks as `any` for free. The repo deliberately does **not** rely on that — it
declares a narrowed intersection type instead:

```ts
// overrides/app/types/commerce.ts:7-10
export type ProductWithSizeFit = NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof useProduct>['data']> & {
  c_sizeFit?: string;
};
```

Used at `product-detail/index.tsx:78` as `(product as ProductWithSizeFit | undefined)?.c_sizeFit`.
**Copy this pattern for every new `c_*` attribute** — add the field to `commerce.ts`, re-export from
`types/index.ts`. It satisfies AGENTS.md > Type Definitions ("don't re-declare types already exported by
`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`") by deriving from `ReturnType<typeof useProduct>` rather than restating it. **[V]**

## 6. Test requirements & what CI actually enforces

### 6a. Storybook a11y — gated. Confirmed still true.

- `.storybook/preview.tsx:34-50` sets `parameters.a11y.test = 'error'`, with an inline comment:
  "'error' causes a11y violations to fail `test-storybook --ci` runs". It also excludes the six Chakra
  toast-manager `role="region"` containers from all a11y checks. **[V]**
- `.storybook/` contains exactly two files: `main.js`, `preview.tsx`. **There is no
  `.storybook/test-runner.js`, and none is needed** — `@storybook/test-runner` v0.24 reads
  `parameters.a11y.test` from `preview.tsx` directly. **[V]**
- `@storybook/test-runner ^0.24.4` and `@storybook/addon-a11y ^10.4.6` are devDependencies;
  the addon is registered at `.storybook/main.js:10`. **[V]**
- `.github/workflows/qa.yml:236-272` job `storybook-test`: builds Storybook, serves `storybook-static`
  on `:6006` via `http-server`, then `node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006`.
  Note it invokes the binary directly — **there is no `test-storybook` npm script** in `package.json`,
  so locally you must run `node_modules/.bin/test-storybook` yourself. **[V]**

### 6b. What `qa.yml` gates (PRs to `develop` and `release/**` only)

| Job | Gated? | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `unit-tests` (Vitest, `npm test`) | **Yes** | `qa.yml:207-227`; runs if any `overrides/**`, `vitest.config.*`, `vitest.setup.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js` changed, or `package.json` `dependencies` changed |
| `storybook-test` (play + a11y) | **Yes** | `qa.yml:236-272`; runs if `overrides/app/{components,pages,hooks,theme,types}/**`, `.storybook/**`, or `package*.json` changed |
| `e2e-localhost` (Playwright, real SFCC dev org) | **Yes** | `qa.yml:280-409` |
| `e2e-browserstack` | Conditional | `qa.yml:427-473`; `release/**` → full suite; `develop` PR → only if an `SFCC-\d+` key appears in PR title/body/branch, `--grep`-scoped to it |
| **ESLint** | **NO** | `grep -rnE 'eslint\|npm run lint' .github/workflows/` → **zero matches across all 15 workflow files** **[V]** |
| **Prettier / `npm run format`** | **NO** | same grep, zero matches. Only local: `.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse `Write` runs `prettier --write` on newly-written files **[V]** |
| **`tsc --noEmit`** | **NO** | same grep, zero matches. It is an AGENTS.md hard requirement enforced by nobody but you **[V]** |

Git hooks in `.husky/` are `commit-msg` (conventional commits), `pre-commit` (registry regen + Contentful
drift + derived-AI-config protection + `.env.sample` secret guard), `pre-push` (tag-name validation).
**None of the three runs lint, prettier, or tsc.** **[V]**

### 6c. E2E scoping — a PDP change runs the FULL suite

`qa.yml:97-102` defines exactly one area allow-list, `e2e_homepage`. There is **no `e2e_pdp` group**,
even though 11 specs already carry `@pdp`. `qa.yml:135-146` narrows to an area only when *every*
e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one area's list — a PDP file never does, so `e2e_scope`
falls back to `full`. That is the deliberate fail-safe direction (more tests, not fewer), not a bug —
but it means every PDP PR pays for the whole Playwright suite. Adding an `e2e_pdp` group is a cheap,
self-contained follow-up. **[V]**

### 6d. What a new PDP component is actually required to have

Per `.claude/rules/testing.md` and `.claude/rules/components.md` > Storybook **[V]**:

| Layer | Required? |
|---|---|
| `*.stories.tsx` | **Yes, always**, for anything exported from its folder under `components/` or `pages/`. Not required for a sub-component that only ever renders inside one parent. Needs a `Default` export; named exports for meaningful states only. |
| `play` fn inside the story | Only when there is interactive behaviour worth asserting (validation on blur, disclosure open/close, focus movement, controlled-input wiring). Purely visual stories need none. Query via `within(canvasElement)`, `getByRole` first. Import `userEvent`/`expect` from the Storybook re-export — `pdpProductInfo/index.stories.tsx:2` uses `from 'storybook/test'`. |
| `*.test.ts` (Vitest) | Only when failure would be non-obvious or costly: data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, pure logic that survives a refactor invisibly. Explicitly **not** for re-exports, one-liners, or framework behaviour. `extractModelLine` is the canonical example of a "yes". |
| `.feature` + Playwright spec | For a new user journey. Gherkin first, **Lead QA signs off the `.feature` before any Playwright is written** (`.claude/skills/qa-generate/`). Tag every `test()` with both `@<area>` and `@SFCC-NNN`. |

Storybook category for PDP components: **`Commerce/`** (`components.md` > Categorisation — "Commerce-specific
shared components"). `Pages/` for the full page assembly. Both already used correctly
(`Commerce/PdpProductInfo`, `Pages/PDP`). `zimmPageToolbar` is a structural/layout wrapper —
**[I]** `Layout/` is arguably the right home for it; it is currently untitled in this analysis because
I did not open its story's `title`. Worth a glance.

Accessibility rules are **mechanically enforced** by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` at PR review:
`<img>` needs `alt`, `IconButton` needs `aria-label`, non-interactive element with `onClick` needs
`role` (+ `tabIndex={0}` + `onKeyDown`). `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap its value in a sanitizer —
enforced by `semgrep.yml`. `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:43,54` already does this with
`DOMPurify.sanitize(...)` from `isomorphic-dompurify`. **[V]**

Things a PDP build should be using rather than rebuilding:

1. **`PdpProductInfo` + its theme recipe** — `overrides/app/components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` and
   `overrides/app/theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts`. Name / price / sanitized description / model
   line / style code, all test-id'd, all styled through `useMultiStyleConfig`. **This is the reference
   implementation of the repo's styling convention** — copy its structure for every new PDP component.

4. **`extractModelLine`** — `overrides/app/utils/productData.ts`, plus its 5 passing tests.
5. **`ProductWithSizeFit`** — `overrides/app/types/commerce.ts`. Extend this file for new `c_*` fields;

6. **`PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH`** — exported from `product-detail/index.tsx:14` and already consumed by
   the story. Any gallery/options layout work should import it, not restate `360px`.
7. **`ProductPage` POM** — `e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js`. Already has `goToProduct()` with the 20s
   SFCC-API gate, `selectVariant()`, `addToCart()`, `getFirstBreadcrumbCategoryLink()`, and locators for
   `product-price` / `product-description` / `product-style-code` / `product-model-info` /
   `sale-price` / `original-price` / `out-of-stock` / `cart-drawer`. **`sale-price`, `original-price`,
   `out-of-stock` and `cart-drawer` locators exist but nothing renders those test-ids yet** — they are a
   pre-agreed contract for the next PDP slice. Use those exact test-ids.
8. **SFCC-91's `pdpColourSwatches`** — 189 lines of component + 256 lines of Vitest + 204 lines of
   stories + an 883-line spec at `.docs/specs/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.md`, plus the multi-colour
   SKU fixture in `e2e/fixtures/products.js`. **Rebase-and-adopt, do not rewrite.** Two caveats: it
   predates the `pdpProductInfo` theme-recipe refactor (rebase conflict guaranteed in
   `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx`), and it needs relocating to `ui-kits/` + a theme recipe to match convention.
9. **`.claude/rules/overrides.md`** on `origin/feature/f2r-component-registry` — the pre-flight checklist
   (default export, internal-consumer grep, `forwardRef`, Chakra deep-merge audit, prop-superset pattern,
   `vendor.d.ts` ambient rule). If PDP work overrides any SFCC component, run that checklist. Consider
   asking for it to be merged to `develop`, since `overrideStyling.md` already links to it and the link
   is currently dead.
10. **`overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts`** — exists, unread in this survey; check it before writing any
    image-URL/resize helper for the gallery. **[I]**

- **The gallery column is a coloured empty box** (`index.tsx:56`). Everything image-related is unbuilt.
- **`overrideStyling.md` vs `uikit-components.md`** — two mutually exclusive styling models on two
  branches (§2c). Get a ruling before writing components.
- **`ui-kits/` has one component and no rules doc on `develop`** (§2b/2c). Both `pdpProductInfo` and

## Condensed findings

**Three premises in the brief turned out to be wrong — flagging first.**

1. **The registry is NOT an unmerged dependency.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, `.claude/registry/*.md` and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` are all on `develop` (`git ls-tree develop` confirms). Not a blocker. It's also fully automatic — components never register themselves (`generateRegistry.mjs:670` classifies `Override` vs `Custom` by folder-name match; `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:49-62` regenerates and stages on every commit).

2. **The ui-kits convention is not settled and is not written down on this branch.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` contains exactly one component — `atoms/zimmPageToolbar/`. No `molecules/`, no `organisms/`. Grepping the whole repo for `ui-kits` returns 3 hits (2 imports + 1 registry row). The rules doc — `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md` — exists only on the unmerged `origin/feature/f2r-implementation-workflow`, **and it directly contradicts `overrideStyling.md` on `develop`**: it *forbids* Chakra inside ui-kit files and mandates per-component `{name}.styles.ts` + Emotion `<Global>`, where `overrideStyling.md` mandates Chakra props + a theme recipe. The two docs never coexist on any branch. This needs a ruling before any component is written.

3. **None of the PDP-adjacent SFCC overrides exist.** `image-gallery`, `swatch-group`, `display-price`, `product-tile`, `product-item`, `recommended-products`, `product-view`, `quantity-picker` — zero files on HEAD *and* on `develop`. `overrideStyling.md` discusses several of them at length as if they exist; it's describing an aspirational state.

**What actually exists for PDP:** a 95-line page (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) that fully replaces the 876-line base — gallery column is an empty placeholder `<Box>` (`:56`), and base's `ProductView`, `RecommendedProducts`, `InformationAccordion`, `<Island>` hydration, `<Helmet>`, `HTTPNotFound`/404 handling, SSR cache headers, and the whole rich `useProduct` expand list are all absent. Plus `pdpProductInfo` (the one component with a proper theme recipe — the reference implementation), `breadcrumb`, `zimmPageToolbar`, `extractModelLine`, `ProductWithSizeFit`, and a `ProductPage` POM with locators already agreed for the *next* slice (`sale-price`, `original-price`, `out-of-stock`, `cart-drawer` — nothing renders those test-ids yet).

**Intercept traps:** (a) real mechanism, confirmed (`.storybook/main.js:25` aliases past the resolver, `vitest.config.ts` never mentions the package) but **not currently triggered** — the only base-path/override collision in the repo is `icons`, and that's deliberate. It goes live the moment PDP overrides `swatch-group`/`image-gallery`/`display-price`/`quantity-picker`, all of which `product-view` imports by base path. (b) confirmed with numbers: the `shared/ui` barrel has 103 relative re-exports, **212** base files import the barrel, **0** import a deep path — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing. PDP doesn't depend on it and shouldn't start. (c) the `_app` checkout swap (`_app/index.jsx:216,484`) never matches `/product/:productId` — **no PDP equivalent exists**.

**Data layer:** `useProduct`/`useCategory` called only in the page (`:21-31`), components are pure — rule obeyed. Type resolves to `ShopperProductsModelTypes.Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783`), everything optional except `id`, with an `& {[key:string]: any}` tail. The repo deliberately doesn't lean on that tail — `ProductWithSizeFit` derives from `ReturnType<typeof useProduct>` and narrows `c_sizeFit` to `string`. Copy that per new `c_*` field.

**CI reality:** Vitest, Storybook (play + a11y), and Playwright are gated. Storybook a11y confirmed still working — `.storybook/preview.tsx:34-36` sets `a11y.test: 'error'`, no `test-runner.js` exists or is needed, `qa.yml:262` invokes the binary directly. **ESLint, Prettier and `tsc --noEmit` are gated nowhere** — `grep -rnE 'eslint|npm run lint|tsc --noEmit|prettier' .github/workflows/` returns zero matches across all 15 workflows, and none of the three husky hooks runs them either. `tsc --noEmit` currently exits 0. Also: `qa.yml` has no `e2e_pdp` allow-list group, so every PDP change falls back to the full Playwright suite.

**Biggest reuse item I'd have missed:** `overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts`'s `proxyImageUrl()` — rewrites SFCC image URLs through the PWA Kit proxy because direct Demandware-host access is Cloudflare-WAF-blocked outside the CC network. Any gallery work that renders `imageGroups[].images[].link` without it will 403 for real shoppers.

Adopt it, don't rewrite it.
